discovery.about: User and contributor documentation for Obscura, published as a GitBook: installation, quickstarts, guides for CLI, CDP, Puppeteer, Playwright, MCP and the Rust library, reference pages and contributor guides.
discovery.see: Documentation landing page: what Obscura is, a comparison table against headless Chrome (memory, binary size, startup, page load), rendering and stealth as first-class features, and links to every quickstart, guide, reference and contributor page.

GitBook table of contents grouping the pages into Quickstart (installation, first fetch, extraction, connecting clients), Guides, Reference (CLI, environment variables) and Contributing sections in reading order.

Installing Obscura from release archives for Linux x86_64 and ARM64, macOS and Windows, the AUR package and the distroless Docker image, archive suffixes for render and stealth variants, a smoke test with --eval and --screenshot, and troubleshooting glibc and Gatekeeper errors.

First steps with obscura fetch: printing rendered HTML, evaluating JavaScript with --eval and JSON output, wrapping multi-statement code in an IIFE because const returns null, waitUntil levels, and common flags such as --timeout, --selector and --proxy.

The --dump output formats explained with examples: html, text, markdown, links, assets as NDJSON including fetch and XHR URLs, original raw server HTML, and cookies including HttpOnly ones, plus combining with --wait-until and piping.

Markdown extraction with --dump markdown: which elements are converted and which stripped, saving to a file, quiet output for RAG and LLM context, waiting for SPA content and narrowing to a region with --selector.

Connecting Puppeteer (puppeteer-core) and Playwright (connectOverCDP) to obscura serve, waitUntil defaults, the supported page API surface including screenshots, PDF and raw screencast, DOMSnapshot support for browser-use, and current limits such as the shared V8 isolate and raster-only PDF.

Detailed Puppeteer guide: connect, navigate, evaluate, interact, cookies, request interception, exposeFunction callbacks, multiple pages, screenshots, scrolling and PDF, raw CDP screencasting, disconnecting and current limits.

Detailed Playwright guide over CDP: connect, navigate, evaluate, SVG element interfaces, interaction and locators, cookies, interception, JS heap measurements, timing, multiple pages, screenshots and PDF, screencasting, fetch cancellation and current limits.

Running obscura mcp over stdio or HTTP for AI agents: security (OBSCURA_MCP_TOKEN bearer, origin allowlist, resource bounds), the full browser_* tool list from navigation and snapshots to forms, screenshots, PDF, cookies, storage and tabs, and Claude Desktop and Claude Code configuration.

Watching an agent's Obscura session live with tools/live-view.mjs: how it polls Page.captureScreenshot instead of screencast, acknowledging frames, one client per page socket, and when to use one-shot screenshots instead.

Embedding the engine with the obscura crate: adding the git dependency, a quickstart, the Page API (goto, content, evaluate, query_selector, wait_for_selector, settle), passive on_request and on_response callbacks, active interception, preload scripts, and when to use the library versus CDP, MCP or CLI.

Intercepting requests through CDP Fetch with Puppeteer and Playwright: blocking by resource type or URL pattern, modifying headers, returning fake responses, stripping analytics, and the equivalent native API in the Rust library.

Persisting cookies and localStorage with --storage-dir: the cookies.json and per-origin localStorage layout, when state is written, logging in once and reusing the session, and running separate identities on different ports.

Stealth mode and proxies: what --stealth changes (wreq TLS fingerprint, tracker blocklist, webpki roots), what it does and does not defeat, HTTP and SOCKS5 proxies with auth, custom user agents, and keeping browser profile, OBSCURA_TIMEZONE and OBSCURA_GEOLOCATION consistent.

Production operations: Docker as uid 65532 and storage permissions, why the container binds 0.0.0.0, systemd units, worker processes, V8 heap sizing, parallel scrape, resource limits, reverse proxy and authentication options, the MCP HTTP transport, observability and timeouts.

Complete CLI reference: global flags, obscura fetch options and --dump formats, --screenshot behavior and adaptive settle, obscura serve options (workers, font dirs, file access), obscura scrape, obscura mcp with token and origin rules, and the obscura-worker NDJSON protocol with navigation status.

Every environment variable: OBSCURA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK and its DNS-time SSRF checks, navigation, chain, script, module, CDP command and fetch timeouts, OBSCURA_CDP_TOKEN, OBSCURA_PROXY, stealth identity variables, MCP token and origins, RUST_LOG, OPENSSL_NO_VENDOR and V8 heap flag defaults.

Building Obscura from source: requirements, render and render plus stealth builds, builds without rendering, BoringSSL prerequisites (CMake, Clang, libclang), a macOS 26 SDK workaround, OPENSSL_NO_VENDOR for AVX-512 errors, installing, and running tests with cargo nextest.

Architecture of the nine-crate workspace: request flow from a CDP Page.navigate through server, dispatch, browser, net, DOM and JS runtime; the rendering flow and retained layout; the single shared V8 isolate and v8_lock; the watchdog; the bootstrap.js and ops.rs bridge; Workers, sessions, lifecycle, storage and stealth.

Two worked recipes: adding a CDP method (handler in obscura-cdp domains, dispatcher match arm, test) and adding a Web API (Rust op in ops.rs, registration in build_extension, JS shim in bootstrap.js, dependency, smoke test), using crypto.subtle.digest as the example.

Testing and debugging: Rust test suites and the fast edit/test loop, CDP parity tests, logging, driving the CDP server by hand, common failure modes (createTarget timeouts, null goto, missing contexts, V8 isolate fatal errors, hangs), reproducing bug reports, rendering regressions and profiling.

Note recording the removal of the repository's three GitHub Actions workflows and their scripts/ci helpers, the resulting loss of hosted PR checks, release builds and Docker Hub publishing, rollback and acceptance criteria.
